newsitem.title: USA: Mobil profits cut by charges; ARCO posts gain.
newsitem.headline: Mobil profits cut by charges; ARCO posts gain.

text.p: Mobil Corp. said Monday its fourth-quarter profits fell nearly $100 million from a year ago because of special charges that included the start-up cost of its European marketing venture with British Petroleum.
Meanwhile, Los Angeles-based Atlantic Richfield Co. said its earnings rose about 10 percent in the latest quarter, capping off one of the most successful years in the company's 130-year history.

Both companies enjoyed strong gains in exploration and production earnings due to higher crude oil and natural gas prices. Those price gains, however, put pressure on refining and marketing earnings by raising feedstock costs.
Mobil said its net income fell to $676 million, or $1.68 a share, on revenues of $23.23 billion vs. year-earlier earnings of $775, or $1.93 a share, on revenues of $20.25 billion.

For the 1996 year, Mobil reported earnings of $3.0 billion, or $7.38 a share, on revenues of $80.78 billion. That compared with 1995 earnings of $2.37 billion, or $5.87 a share, on revenues of $75.37 billion.

The Fairfax, Va.-based company said its results for the latest quarter included a charge of $145 million to cover the start-up costs of a previously announced European marketing venture with British Petroleum.

It said exploration and production profits for the latest quarter jumped $306 million to a record $649 million. But earnings from marketing and refining fell $116 million to $256 million because of the higher cost of buying energy products.
Mobil said its chemicals unit's profits fell $59 million to $81 million for the quarter partly due to lower petrochemical margins.
Mobil's stock was up $1.375 at $130 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Arco said its fourth-quarter earnings rose to $380 million, or $2.32 a share, from $348 million, or $2.13 a share a year earlier. Revenues increased to $5.24 billion from $4.22 billion.
Arco attributed the rise in profits to sharply higher earnings in its exploration and production division, which were offset by losses in its refining and market operations.
"Strong oil and natural gas prices helped our performance, but increases in production and cost control also contributed to a fine year, said Mike Bowlin, Arco's chairman and chief executive officer.

The company said its exploration and production unit, responsible for finding and pumping oil around the world, earned $406 million in the fourth quarter, compared with $163 million in the year-ago quarter.
The rise in crude oil prices hurt its refining and marketing business. The unit had a fourth quarter loss of $8 million compared with a profit of $53 million a year earlier.
Higher costs in crude oil can be a boon for production divisions while depressing earnings at the gasoline pump.
Analysts said a harsh price war in the southern California gasoline market hurt fourth quarter results, but Arco officials said it was only one of several factors hitting its bottom line.
"We're not singling that out," said a company spokesman. "Los Angeles is an important part of the (gasoline) market, but it's not the only part."
For all of 1996, Arco earned $1.7 billion, or $10.18 a share, vs. $1.4 billion, or $8.42 a share in 1995. Revenues for the year rose to $19.2 billion from $16.7 billion.
Arco's stock was off $2.125 to $133.625 on the NYSE.
